question.text: Let <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> are <math><mn>2</mn></math> non-zero and non-collinear vectors, then the largest value of <math><mi>k</mi></math> such that the non-zero vectors <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msup><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mfenced><mover><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced><mover><mi>y</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math><mn>2</mn><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> are collinear is

solution.text:
Let, a→=k2-5k+6x→+k-3y→
and b→=2x→+5y→
∵a→ and b→ are collinear vectors
⇒k2-5k+62=k-35
⇒k=3,125 

But, for k=3, a→=0 (not possible)
